articles.title: CAS wild swing: Sensex soars 1,000 points on expiry day but ends only 138 points higher
articles.summary: In a surprising turnaround, India's stock market indices, Sensex and Nifty, erased intraday losses to close positively on Thursday. articles.title: Brent crosses $100 as West Asia war raises pressure on India’s economy
articles.summary: Brent crude surpassed $100 due to escalating conflict in West Asia, raising concerns over India's rising oil import bill. India, reliant on oil imports, may face increased inflation and fiscal challenges amid an already significant surge in prices and global market instability.
articles.why: India imports about 85% of its crude. Every $10 on Brent adds roughly 0.3-0.4 percentage points to inflation and widens the current account deficit, which is why stocks, bonds and the rupee all fell together.

articles.title: Rupee slumps 38 paise to close at 95.46 against US dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee slipped by 38 paise, settling at 95.46 against the US dollar on Thursday, influenced by Brent crude oil prices rising above USD 102 per barrel. Forex traders highlighted conflicting factors affecting the currency, such as portfolio outflows alongside costly crude prices. While the dollar index…
articles.why: A weaker rupee raises the cost of fuel, electronics and foreign education, and squeezes companies with dollar debt. Exporters, notably IT and pharma, are the relative winners.

articles.title: ECB prepares for ‘longer-lasting’ inflation as it lifts interest rates to 2.5%
articles.summary: Central bank president Christine Lagarde warns price shock driven by Middle East conflict will persist well into 2027
articles.why: Europe is now in a hiking cycle again, with Lagarde warning the energy shock lasts into 2027. Higher global rates make it harder for the RBI to ease and keep foreign money flowing out of emerging markets.

articles.title: Hotter producer prices strengthen bets on a Fed rate hike
articles.summary: US producer prices rose, increasing rate hike expectations for the Federal Reserve. Traders now price a seventy percent chance of a quarter-point increase next week. articles.title: RBI announces 26-day VRRR auction to absorb Rs 5 lakh crore surplus liquidity
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India plans a significant 26-day auction this Friday, targeting the withdrawal of Rs 5 lakh crore from the inter-bank market. This extended operation aims to manage persistent liquidity by giving participants the chance to reclaim lent amounts. This proactive measure is a direct response to the…
articles.why: Banks are sitting on a record cash surplus. Draining ₹5 lakh crore for 26 days nudges short-term rates up and signals the RBI is worried about inflation, not growth, for now.

articles.title: India August consumer inflation likely hit 20-month high on food, fuel prices: Reuters poll
articles.summary: India faces an anticipated spike in consumer inflation, predicting a high not seen in 20 months this August. Rising food and fuel prices are at the forefront of this increase, as the trend of surpassing the Reserve Bank of India's inflation target continues for the third month. Additionally, global crude oil and…

articles.title: India bonds face twin drag from rising oil, US yields

articles.title: Treasury yields surge toward the danger zone for stocks, as inflation pressures heat up
articles.summary: Oil prices were at their highest levels since late May, while rising wholesale inflation data sent benchmark 10-year yields closer to the key 5% level.
articles.why: A 5% US 10-year yield is the level where equity valuations tend to break, historically. It is the single most important number for global risk appetite right now.

articles.title: Sebi launches Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenised corporate bonds
articles.summary: Sebi has launched Demat 2.0, a pilot for tokenised corporate bonds using distributed ledger technology and wholesale e-rupee settlement. REC, L&T and IIFL have raised Rs 1,025 crore, while future phases will enable trading and retail investor access in India.
articles.why: Tokenised bonds settled in wholesale e-rupee are a real-world test of blockchain plumbing. If retail access follows, corporate bond investing could get as easy as buying a stock.

articles.title: CAS stays, but derivatives settlement may change, says Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey after another 1,000-point Sensex swing

articles.title: India’s merchandise exports jump 15% despite global headwinds: Piyush Goyal

articles.title: RBI uses currency swaps to cut $115 billion cash surplus
articles.summary: India's central bank is draining excess cash from banks using currency swaps. This action follows record high funds in the financial system. articles.why: Selling dollars for rupees does two jobs at once: it props up the rupee and soaks up excess cash. The scale ($115 billion) shows how much foreign inflow the system absorbed earlier this year.
